pr_body:
This PR adds a preview box like github does for permalinks to a range of lines for a file in the repo, e.g: `http://localhost:3000/mai-lapyst/testprojet_ci/src/commit/49fb6d29fad1933818f06eef1bf95f6d7235f3f6/some/deep/folder/test.js#L7-L19`.

Closes #20359.

This works in both issues/PRs, as well as other markup rendering for example markdown files.
It's implemented as a processor in `modules/markup/html.go`.

It also supports the unicode warnings the "normal" code view of files inside the repo support, as shown in the example rendering.

Example renderings:
![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/67418776/2c138471-5c29-41a3-b4dc-4ac7d3133b8c)

![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/67418776/ac6c573a-114f-45f8-ae0e-e0df3ad436bc)
pr_comments: Does this yellow triangle render the same in normal code view? If not, I think it may be using some overly-specific CSS selector that fixes it only for the normal code view.

> > > Does this yellow triangle render the same in normal code view? If not, I think it may be using some overly-specific CSS selector that fixes it only for the normal code view. It seems the exact same for me in testing. Could'nt find a specific css on the normal code view, even after rebasing onto main.
Please add some tests for newly introduced regex and the function.
Maybe it can also support branches and tags files but not commits only.

> Please add some tests for newly introduced regex and the function.

Have added the requested test.

> Maybe it can also support branches and tags files but not commits only.

It would advise against it. These file previews are commonly used with permalinks to discuss a certain state in the codebase and thus need to refer to the state of those files in the moment the issue takes place. Using "dynamic" links, such as a branch or tag, where a commit isnt fixed, can lead to confusion since later the file contains not that what was talked about.
Needs a merge in `services/markup/processorhelper.go`. After that is fixed, I will test it.

issue_context.title: Inline code references
issue_context.body:
### Feature Description

I think it would be great if gitea has some inline-code reference feature like github does. Currently only an link is rendered in gitea.

### Screenshots

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67418776/178816020-6b276ac2-3695-4ea3-90ae-c640de36d2c6.png)
comments: Were there any progress on this?

review_comments: Add a `muted` class to this to uncolor it.

Should this too be applied for the second link to the commit itself?

Rendering with only muted on the first link:

![grafik](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/67418776/1e2b118a-e392-425f-8e78-0d3abff06bdf)
Yes, but in this case I would say add `text grey` classes to the parent element that holds the "Lines..." text and `text black` classes to the link so that it stands out a bit.
This seems too brittle. I wonder if we can somehow bypass the sanitizer completely for node and all its children, ideally still forbidding all these attributes from user content.

Yeah I thought so too. It's also why I made the button added in the PR an `<a>` to not allow `<button>`'s from user content.

The problem is that all postprocessing is applied before the sanitizer is called, and since all the `*html.Node` is written to a writer and thus looks like normal / user-created html, theres no simple way to distinguish generated html and user-provided one.

It might be possible to do two postprocessing passes, one before and one after sanitizing, or to move post processing after the santizing step since all post processing is declared inside go so there should no risk here, atleast if each postprocessing step takes some care to escape / sanitize any outside input themself.
I see. I guess it is acceptable for now with the current method, but this is definitely something we need to do eventually.
